verdicts.reason: Both put the CTA at the very top, ahead of the headline (reading order is wrong), and set 'Now in 4-packs and singles' larger than the body copy, which inverts the hierarchy. A also jams the CTA about 12px from the top edge and packs the headline tight against the body, while B has slightly better margins and larger type.

A has the CTA crammed into the top corner before the headline, the headline butts against the body, and the secondary line is oversized. B reads in the right order (logo, headline, product, CTA), but the headline and body sit over the decorative circle, there is a dead gap under the product, and the small CTA is crushed against the legal line at the bottom.

A opens with the CTA, wedges the headline right under it over the circle, and leaves a big empty band below the product. B has a sensible top-to-bottom order and a larger product, but the circle is a clutter behind the copy, the secondary line is still bigger than the body, and the CTA is jammed against the legal at the bottom edge.

A is a real rearrangement with readable type, but the CTA is placed first, above the headline, and the secondary line is oversized compared with the body. B is just the square original shrunk into a strip: the logo, legal text and secondary line are unreadably small, and there are huge dead areas at the top and bottom, so it fails fit-to-format.
